top.line: Every article reviewed on the record, never twice
top.para: One model writes these articles and some things fall through, so they get reviewed as records: published criteria any reviewer reads, one file per article and text, five at a time, newest first, each finding answered on the article. The editor and the desk use the same record, and signed readers come next.

in-short.line: Criteria, records, batches, answers, on every page
in-short.para: Published criteria cover facts, voice, claims, conversions, health and people. A review is one file per article, text and reviewer, so nothing is reviewed twice; reviewers take five, newest first. The newsroom answers every finding and every article shows its reviews. The editor and desk use the same record; signed readers are next.

why.line: One model writes, so a second reader checks
why.para: Publishing works, and an article has become a way to answer people. But one model with a lot of context misses things, like today's superlative caught only because I read it. So every article gets a second pass by readers that are not the writer: other models, then me and the desk, cheap enough to run when credits allow.

criteria.line: Six published questions any reviewer answers
criteria.para: The criteria are published as a page and as markdown. Facts against sources; voice, including what I would not say; claims and limits; conversions and translations; the article's health today; and people. Each is pass, issues or not checked, and each finding has a severity, section, exact quote, evidence and the smallest fix.

record.line: Reviewer, article and text hash: never twice
record.para: A review is one immutable file in the article's folder, tied to a hash of the article's sections. A reviewer never gets the same text twice: it takes its next five, newest first, from a status file, reads its own past reviews and the answers first, and leaves. That makes review a background job rather than a project.

arrives.line: A pull request, a commit, by hand, or a vault
arrives.para: Outside agents send a pull request touching only review files, checked before it is merged; agents in the repository commit after the same check; one with no access hands the JSON to the editor. Later, the editor's channel append lane lets a reviewer send without an account, sealed to the newsroom.

answers.line: Every finding answered, every article shows reviews
answers.para: The newsroom answers each finding in a status file only it writes: fixed with the version, declined with the reason, or open. The hub lists open findings, the daily pass works through them, and each article now has a Reviews section showing who, when, which version, the verdict and the findings' fate.

people.line: The editor, the desk and later signed readers
people.para: This is comments on the record, not a comments section. My sign-off is an approval at a version; disagreement is a comment with a finding; journalists will review the same way. Notes can be added years later, such as I got this wrong, keeping articles alive. Signed readers who confirm or dispute are next.

first-run.line: Five reviews, eighteen findings, all fixed
first-run.para: Another model from the writer's vendor reviewed the five newest articles in about nineteen minutes: one approval, four with changes, 18 findings, 4 medium and 14 low. The medium ones were real, a misattributed quote among them. All were checked and fixed in this release, and its notes on the criteria became version 1.1.

limits.line: Review makes checks visible, not articles right
limits.para: Review shows what was checked and found; it does not make an article right. One model has reviewed one batch, and the criteria are version 1.1. Findings are claims to check. A hash is not a signature, nothing reviews the reviewers yet, and signed readers are a proposal.

sources.line: A voice memo, the criteria and the code
sources.para: From a voice memo on 18 October 2026. The criteria at /reviews/criteria.md, written from the article guide and the wording check; the status file at /reviews/status.json; the code in admin/build/reviews.py; with related articles on the editor's channel, undo cost, the human in the loop and agent policies.
